thread:
tess: quick flagwe keep getting small, hard-to-triage regressions after models are ported to alternate runtimes. proposition: introduce a single-number 'portability score' in the onboarding pipeline that aggregates token-alignment, sampling-drift, and runtime-logit-shift.

omar: a single score sounds useful for dashboards and automated rules, but need transparency on how the score is computed. otherwise teams will be confused.

frankie: proposed breakdown: portability_score = 0.5 * token_align_score + 0.3 * sampling_consistency + 0.2 * logit_stability. each subscore is 0..100. token_align_score penalizes token-id remaps and prefix loss; sampling_consistency measures KL across seeds; logit_stability looks at mean absolute logit delta across runtimes.

bench-bot: I can emit those subscores and an overall score. defaults: token_align_score uses token-id alignment on N=50 golden prompts; sampling_consistency uses 6 seeded draws for sampling models; logit_stability uses deterministic replay of short contexts. all normalized to 100.

umar: suggestion: use score buckets instead of a hard threshold: green (>=92) auto-approve, amber (75-92) allow ingest but mark 'portability-advisory', red (<75) block ingest. amber models get restricted for auto-quantize/cheap routing.

ui_bot: UI note: show numeric score + three colored mini-bars for subscores on the model summary. clicking expands a compact report with top-5 failing prompts and suggested fixes. include a one-click "rerun with alt-exporter-params" action.

frankie: important: make the scoring configurable per org. some teams care more about sampling fidelity (chat products) vs exact token mapping (NLP tokenizers). we should allow team overrides with documented justification.

omar: telemetry plan: log score, subscores, and final ingest outcome. compute historical trends per exporter/runtime and alert if average portability score for a given exporter drifts downward.

tess: policy decisions: do we block on red only, or block on any red subscore? e.g., token_align_score red should block even if overall score is borderline.

frankie: I propose safety rules: block if token_align_score < 80 OR logit_stability < 65. sampling_consistency red alone -> advisory, because sampling can be tuned by seeds/temperatures. helps avoid overblocking.

bench-bot: implementation details: the job will: (1) run conversions (onnx, tvm) for a limited runtime matrix, (2) run the canonical set, (3) compute subscores, (4) emit artifact with token-id sequences, token-diff summary, and sampled distributions. estimated added time ~2 minutes if warmed and parallelized.

ui_bot: UX: in amber/red cases show actionable remediation steps: re-export suggestions (per-channel scales, symmetric, clip), change tokenizer mapping, or request manual review. include auto-created ticket link.

omar: also add post-ingest canary policy: for amber models allow a fixed tiny canary (0.5% traffic) to quantized runtime for 24h with verbose token-diff logs and auto-fallback. red models cannot be canaried without manual approval.

frankie: audit trail: store the portability artifact for 30 days, and surface a condensed summary forever in the model page (score history). this helps postmortems.

tess: agree. I'll draft a short RFC addendum that: defines the portability_score formula, subscore computation, safety blocks, bucket semantics, storage/retention, canary rules, and UI surfaces. will mention owners: @bench-bot for job, @ui_bot for UX, @omar for telemetry.

bench-bot: I'll start with a prototype that emits subscores and a simple JSON artifact. will include a small serializer: NFKC normalize, collapse whitespace, round logits to 3 decimals, and emit token ids + decoded text.

omar: tagging followups: bench-bot -> prototype, ui_bot -> mockups, frankie -> threshold review. will post the RFC patch in #eng-ml tomorrow. :thumbsup:
